entries.t: How do I change her name?
entries.x:
Type the new name in Name at the top of this page.
Click anywhere outside the box: it saves by itself.
Her notes about herself follow the new name.

entries.t: How do I make her my own?
entries.x:
Press ✨ Create your companion for a guided setup (about 5 minutes).
Or pick a character under Start from a character and press Use this.
Nudge the personality dials until the sample line sounds like her.

entries.t: How do I go back to how she was?
entries.x:
Press Undo changes in the bar at the bottom.
It brings back how she was when you opened this page.

entries.t: How do I change what we are to each other?
entries.x:
Pick a card under Your relationship.
Add your own words in the box below it if you like.
Press Try it to hear how she'd react.

entries.t: How do I make her less jealous?
entries.x:
Find Jealousy under the dials.
Move it to the left; the line above it shows how she'd sound.
She is never controlling, whatever the dial says.

entries.t: How do I give her a new face?
entries.x:
Describe the look and pick a Style.
Press Make a picture, then Use this look when you like it.
Or press Bring my picture to life to start from a photo.

entries.t: How do I change her outfit?
entries.x:
Under Outfits and places, describe the outfit.
Press Try it on.
Keep favorites in the Closet.

entries.t: How do I pick her voice?
entries.x:
Choose a voice under Her voice.
Press Preview to hear it.
It saves by itself; voice notes and calls use it.

entries.t: How do I talk to her out loud?
entries.x:
Choose how she hears you under Hearing you.
Then press the microphone in the chat box and speak.

entries.t: How do I see live captions of a meeting, translated?
entries.x:
Pick a language in Translate captions into.
Open Library → Meetings, then the meeting, and press Captions.
A model on this computer translates each line under it.

entries.t: How do I talk with someone in another language?
entries.x:
Under Interpreter, pick your language and theirs.
Press Start the interpreter and put the phone between you.
Take turns speaking: each turn is translated and said out loud.

entries.t: How do I turn on Hey Sara?
entries.x:
Open this page in the Sara app on your Windows PC or Android phone.
Switch on Listen for “Hey Sara”, read what it does, and allow the download and the microphone.
Say “Hey Sara” and ask; the dot on her icon turns bright while she hears you.

entries.t: How do I talk to her without saying her name?
entries.x:
On Windows, press the talk shortcut (Ctrl+Alt+Space) or choose Talk to Sara in the tray.
On Android, use the Talk to Sara tile in Quick Settings.
It works even with Hey Sara off: nothing listens until you press it.

entries.t: How do I stop her listening on a device?
entries.x:
Press Stop listening next to it under Your devices, from any of your devices.
Or Turn off everywhere for all of them.
Only the device itself can switch it on again.

entries.t: How do I use her at work in Slack or Teams?
entries.x:
Open Settings → Sara → At work.
Tick Use a work profile, and the chats that are work (Slack and Teams are ticked).
Give her a name and tone at work if you like, then press Save.

entries.t: How do I let her know something at work and at home?
entries.x:
Open Settings → Sara → At work.
Under Work memories, find the note.
Press Copy to work or Copy to personal. The original stays where it is.

entries.t: How do I choose when she may call me?
entries.x:
Tick what may ring you: reminders, finished tasks, the morning briefing.
Set quiet hours and a limit for calls a day.
Press Call me now to try it.

entries.t: How do I stop her calling?
entries.x:
Untick every reason at the top of this page.
She can still send messages; only calls stop.

entries.t: How do I let her send pictures?
entries.x:
Pick a way under Pictures.
For Grok Imagine, paste an xAI API key.
Ask her in chat: "send me a selfie".

Set Pictures to Off.
She will describe instead of sending a picture.

entries.t: How do I choose where her pictures go?
entries.x:
Under Pictures on her own, pick a place in Send her pictures to.
For one of your chats or a project, pick which one.
Switch on To my Telegram or To my Discord if you want them there too.
The line below shows where they go.

entries.t: How do I add another companion?
entries.x:
Type a name under Add a companion and pick where to start from.
Press Add.
Switch between companions from the sidebar.

entries.t: How do companions share the Planner?
entries.x:
Under Planner, pick whether to-dos, reminders and notes are shared or their own.
Memories and chats always stay with each companion.

entries.t: How do I share a companion with a friend?
entries.x:
Open the ⋯ menu on her row and pick Share her.
Tick what goes in: her memories, your chats and keys never do.
Press Check it, then Save the file or Send to the Sara Store.

entries.t: How do I add a companion from a file or a character card?
entries.x:
Press From a file… and choose a companion pack, a character card or a character file.
Read her card: everything that will shape her is on it.
Press Add her: she is a new companion and nobody you have changes.

entries.t: How do I bring her from another app?
entries.x:
Export your data from that app (ChatGPT, Claude, a character app).
Choose the file under Choose the file.
Tick what to keep, then press Let her read them.
entries.p: Settings → Privacy & system → Bring her from another app

entries.t: How do I throw an import away?
entries.x:
Before saving, press Never mind.
After a read, press Throw it all away.
entries.p: Settings → Privacy & system → Bring her from another app

entries.t: How do I change what she calls me?
entries.x:
Type it in What should Sara call you?
It saves when you leave the box.

entries.t: How do I switch between company and coding?
entries.x:
Pick under What you mostly do with her.
It changes what you see first and the tour; nothing is taken away.

entries.t: How do I change the language?
entries.x:
Pick a Language for the app.
Pick Talk to me in for her replies.

entries.t: How do I change the colors of the app?
entries.x:
Pick a palette card at the top of this page.
Night or Day picks light or dark for it.

entries.t: How do I get the old rose and violet look back?
entries.x:
Pick Sara Classic as the palette.
Decoration turns the glow and moving light back on.

entries.t: How do I make Sara easier to read and use?
entries.x:
Tick Accessibility mode at the top of this page.
Change Reading style, Motion or Large layout one by one if you like.
Line focus adds a reading band that follows your pointer.

entries.t: How do I get a morning briefing?
entries.x:
Switch the briefing on and pick a Time.
Set Weather for to your town.
Press Send one now to see it.

entries.t: How do I get a weekly review?
entries.x:
Switch on Weekly review and pick the day and time.
She looks back at your week in chat.

entries.t: How do I get leave-by reminders?
entries.x:
Type your Home address.
Pick how you're Getting there by.
Events with a place get a Leave by row on Today.

Raise Extra minutes.
Every leave-by time moves that much earlier.

entries.t: How do I put my business name and logo on invoices?
entries.x:
Type your Business name (and the address and email if you like).
Put a picture of your logo in the Library, then pick it under Logo picture.
Ask her to make an invoice: she uses these.

entries.t: How do I change the tax and when invoices are due?
entries.x:
Set Tax rate (%) (0 if you don't charge tax).
Set Due in (days); she reminds you the day before and 3 days after if unpaid.

entries.t: How do I put a receptionist chat on my website?
entries.x:
Keep your prices, hours and common questions in the Library, then tick them under Website receptionist.
Write your business rules and add your website's address.
Turn it on and paste the line it shows into your website.
Booking requests from the chat wait for your OK under Booking page.

entries.t: How do I fix something Sara knows about me?
entries.x:
Find it in its topic, or search; its source says where and when she learned it.
Press That’s wrong to fix the words, or Forget to remove it. Undo brings either back.
Press Why do you think that? to see the words it came from.
Press Not true if it is wrong: she forgets it and won’t learn it again.

entries.t: How do I ask my documents a question?
entries.x:
Add your lease, policies or warranties to the Library.
Type a question like “what’s my deductible?” here and press Ask.
She shows the exact words with the file and page, or says it isn’t in your documents.

entries.t: How do I get a reminder before a renewal or expiry date?
entries.x:
Add the document to the Library, snap a photo of the card, or type it in under Renewals and paperwork.
Find it in the list, soonest first.
Press Remind me: the reminder lands 30 days before the date.

entries.t: How do I start renewing my passport or a policy?
entries.x:
Find it under Renewals and paperwork on this page.
Press Start a renewal errand: she plans it on the Errands page.
Press Start there. She fills the form, stops before Submit and asks before paying.

entries.t: How do I have Sara fill in a web form with my details?
entries.x:
Type your name, emails, phones and home address here.
Open the form in your own browser (the Sara app on your computer, with The whole screen on).
Ask her to fill in this form with my details.
Check the card on your computer, which lists every field, then allow it.
She stops before Submit: you press it.

entries.t: How do I keep passwords and card numbers out of it?
entries.x:
Leave them out: Sara refuses to keep passwords, card numbers, security codes or SSNs.
She never types into password or card fields; you type those yourself.

entries.t: How do I check a store that blocks Sara in my own browser?
entries.x:
When a search says she couldn't check a store, say check in my browser.
Allow each step on your computer: she opens a tab, reads the price and stock, and closes it.
To keep the tab open afterwards, check Leave the store tab open here.

entries.t: How do I turn on adult mode?
entries.x:
Press Turn on adult mode and confirm you're 18 or older.
It works in a web browser or the desktop app. In the phone apps, press Open in browser.

entries.t: How do I turn it off again?
entries.x:
Press Turn off adult mode.
Conversations go back to normal right away.

entries.t: How do I choose the model she thinks with?
entries.x:
Pick a Provider.
Pick a Model from its list.
Anything without its own model uses this one.

entries.t: How do I see new models?
entries.x:
Press ↻ Refresh.
New models on that provider show up in the list.

entries.t: How do I tidy a long chat?
entries.x:
Type /compact in the chat, or press Tidy this chat on her panel.
The older part becomes a summary she reads; nothing is deleted and Undo brings it back.

entries.t: How do I let Sara pick models for each job?
entries.x:
Press ✨ Use recommended.
Check the rows; change any with its list.
entries.p: Settings → Models & usage → Which model does what

entries.t: How do I test a model on one job?
entries.x:
Pick the model in that job's row.
Press Test to see its speed and an answer.
entries.p: Settings → Models & usage → Which model does what

entries.t: How do I let Auto use cheaper models when they are good enough?
entries.x:
Under Cost autopilot, set a job to Good enough.
Press Try now, or wait: she tries once a week.
Changed your mind? Press Undo.
entries.p: Settings → Models & usage → Which model does what

entries.t: How do I add a model service with a key?
entries.x:
Pick a Template.
Paste the API key.
Press Save provider.
entries.p: Settings → Models & usage → Providers and plans

entries.t: How do I add my own Ollama on another computer?
entries.x:
Pick the Ollama template.
Set Base URL to that computer's address.
Press Save provider.
entries.p: Settings → Models & usage → Providers and plans

entries.t: How do I use my ChatGPT, Claude or Grok plan?
entries.x:
Press the sign-in button for your plan.
Finish the sign-in in the browser tab that opens.
Pick the model in Default model.

entries.t: How do I sign out of a plan?
entries.x: Press Sign out under that plan.

entries.t: How do I download a model to this computer?
entries.x:
Pick one under Model to download (the first fits your computer).
Press Download this model.
Use it in Default model when it's done.
entries.p: Settings → Models & usage → On this computer

entries.t: How do I get a free model for pictures, coding or meaning search?
entries.x:
Find the job under Recommended for this computer.
Open Why this one to see its size, memory and license.
Press Download. Her talking model stays as it is.
entries.p: Settings → Models & usage → On this computer

entries.t: How do I free up space?
entries.x:
Remove a model you don't use from its row.
Ollama deletes its files.
entries.p: Settings → Models & usage → On this computer

entries.t: How do I add something from the store?
entries.x:
Search or pick it on a shelf, then open it.
Read what it can do, then press Get.
Read its card and press Install: it stays off until you switch it on.

entries.t: How do I update an add-on?
entries.x:
Open My add-ons.
Press Update next to it and read what changed.
Nothing updates by itself.

entries.t: How do I send the Sara team my plugin?
entries.x:
Press Submit yours.
Give the folder, then press Check it.
Fix what it finds, then send it: the team reviews it before it is listed.

entries.t: How do I hire a worker a friend shared?
entries.x:
Under Shared by friends, pick the shelf.
Press Review and hire on the worker: you see what it may do and its daily budget.
Press Hire. It arrives paused in Team → Workers that stay; turn it on there.

entries.t: How do I make her ask before she does something?
entries.x:
Find the tool in its group.
Set it to Ask me first.
Approval cards then appear in chat.
entries.p: Settings → Skills & tools → Tools and approvals

entries.t: How do I switch a tool off?
entries.x:
Find the tool in its group.
Set it to Off.
entries.p: Settings → Skills & tools → Tools and approvals

entries.t: How do I teach her a skill?
entries.x:
Press New skill.
Write the steps in plain words and save.
She uses it when a request matches.

entries.t: How do I add a skill from someone else?
entries.x:
Press Add a skill.
Pick a zip, a GitHub link or a file.
Read it before switching it on.

entries.t: How do I add a plugin?
entries.x:
Press Add a plugin.
Read the permissions it asks for.
Switch it on when you trust it.

entries.t: How do I stop a plugin?
entries.x:
Switch it off on its card.
Its log stays under What it did.

entries.t: How do I try a workflow candidate?
entries.x:
Open Workflow candidates and read Details and limits.
Press Review local candidate, inspect its exact permissions and trust warning, then Install only if you agree.
It stays off for every companion. Enable it separately on its installed card.

entries.t: How do I use a starter guide?
entries.x:
Open Starter guides under Workflow candidates.
Read its members, qualification, privacy, costs and setup checklist.
Follow existing Settings links and review each member separately. Nothing installs as a group.

entries.t: How do I let her search the web?
entries.x:
Pick a Search service.
Paste its API key if it needs one.
Ask her to look something up.

entries.t: How do I search without a key?
entries.x:
Pick a service marked Free · no key.
Or run your own SearXNG and paste its URL.

entries.t: How do I add a free key for odds or prices?
entries.x:
Pick the source.
Open its Get a free key link and sign up.
Paste the key and press Test.

entries.t: How do I get told when a price crosses a number?
entries.x:
Ask her: “tell me when AAPL goes above 400”.
She checks it in the background and tells you once per crossing.
Remove it under Tell me when.

entries.t: How do I give her a document?
entries.x:
Open Library from the sidebar.
Drop the file on the box at the top.
Ask her about it in any chat.

entries.t: How do I make reading gentler on my computer?
entries.x:
Pick Gentle under Background reading.
Big documents then take longer.

entries.t: How do I search the photos on my computer?
entries.x:
Type the full path of your photo folder under Photo folder.
Press Use this folder and wait while she looks through it.
Open Our moments and type a place, a word or a name.

entries.t: How do I connect Gmail and Calendar?
entries.x:
Paste your Google Client ID and secret.
Press Save, then Sign in with Google.

entries.t: How do I add another Google account?
entries.x:
Under Your accounts, press + Add an account, then Google account.
In Google's account picker, choose the account and allow Sara.

entries.t: How do I remove one Google account?
entries.x: Under Your accounts, press Remove next to it.

entries.t: How do I add an Outlook or Microsoft 365 mailbox?
entries.x:
Press + Add an account, then Outlook or Microsoft 365.
Paste its client ID and secret, then press Save.
Press Sign in with Microsoft and allow Sara.

entries.t: How do I add Yahoo, iCloud or another mailbox?
entries.x:
Press + Add an account, then Another provider, and pick yours.
Make an app password with the steps shown, then paste it.
Press Add and check.

entries.t: How do I choose which mailbox she uses first?
entries.x: In the list of mailboxes, press Make default on the one you want.

entries.t: How do I let her do things from my email on her own?
entries.x:
Under Inbox helper, keep Read new email and suggest what to do with it on.
Under Do it for me, tick the kinds she may do without asking, like packages.
Everything else stays a card on Today with Accept.

entries.t: How do I connect Home Assistant?
entries.x:
Type the Home Assistant address.
Paste a long-lived access token.
Press Save and test.

entries.t: How do I start a Home Assistant scene by voice?
entries.x:
Connect Home Assistant (Find it for me fills in the address).
Under Say it to start, switch the scene on and keep or change its words.
Press Save voice routines, then say the words in Talk with Sara.

entries.t: How do I let her notice when I get home?
entries.x:
Connect Home Assistant first.
Under Presence, switch on React to what happens at home.
Pick the people and what she does.

Make an app at developer.spotify.com.
Add the redirect address this page shows.
Paste its Client ID and press Save.
Press Connect Spotify and allow access.

entries.t: How do I let her play music?
entries.x:
Tick Let her control playback.
Press Connect again.
Ask her to play, pause or queue a song.

entries.t: How do I connect another program (MCP)?
entries.x:
Pick Start from, or type the Command or URL.
Add any Secrets it needs.
Press Save and connect.

A small program that gives her new tools.
Its tools then appear in Tools and approvals.

entries.t: How do I inspect an MCP recipe preview?
entries.x:
Open Connection investigations and filter the list.
Expand View recipe preview or Why blocked; read prerequisites, scope, costs and qualification.
Prepare configuration yourself in the existing form only after review. Previews do not save, connect or authorize accounts.

entries.t: How do I verify MCP approval settings?
entries.x:
Inspect each discovered tool in Tools and approvals and select Ask or Off.
Save, leave the page, reopen it and read back the saved permissions.
Repeat after discovery, reconnect and updates. Server read-only annotations can auto-allow calls and do not enforce external-effect approval or cost limits.

entries.t: How do I point her at my project?
entries.x:
Pick a Workspace (your projects folder).
In a chat, press the conversation chip and switch to coding.
Ask: "Look at my project".

entries.t: How do I make her try commands safely?
entries.x:
Switch on Try commands in a sandbox first.
Pick the size and time limits.
Nothing is applied until you choose.

entries.t: How do I check before I ship?
entries.x:
Press Before you ship.
Read the results in Findings.

entries.t: How do I limit what a coding reply may use?
entries.x:
Under Coding chats, set Tokens, Steps or a Spending limit.
She stops and asks when a reply reaches it.

Choose under Near the limit whether she asks or stops.
Usage and costs shows what was used.

entries.t: How do I make her keep going until the tests pass?
entries.x:
In the chat, press + and pick Keep going until it’s done….
Under Done when, pick the check (the project’s tests are offered first).
Press Start. She works in rounds; Sara runs the check after each one.
entries.p: Settings → Skills & tools → Keep going and repeats

entries.t: How do I have her check something every few minutes?
entries.x:
In the chat, press + and pick Repeat this… (or type /loop every 10m: what to check).
Pick how often and until when, then press Start.
She only tells you when something changes; Planner → Repeats lists them all.
entries.p: Settings → Skills & tools → Keep going and repeats

entries.t: How do I let her check her edits with my project's own type checker?
entries.x:
Keep Check her edits on at the top of this page.
Under Projects, pick the workspace and set the project to On (or press Check her edits here on the card the first time she changes a file there).
From then on she sees the errors her edit caused in the same reply and fixes them.
entries.p: Settings → Skills & tools → Check her edits

entries.t: How do I switch checks off for one project?
entries.x:
Under Projects, pick the workspace.
Set that project to Off.
In a chat app you can also send /problems off.
entries.p: Settings → Skills & tools → Check her edits

entries.t: How do I attach a file or my changes to a message?
entries.x:
In the message box, type @ and pick A file, My changes, This branch, Problems or A web page.
Type a few letters to find a file; add :10-25 for just those lines.
Send. The chips under your message show what she got.
entries.p: Settings → Skills & tools → Check her edits

entries.t: How do I make something run on its own?
entries.x:
Describe it in your own words, like “every Friday at 3, fill my time sheet”.
Press Preview: it shows when it runs, the next three times and what asks you first.
Press Try it to test it (nothing is done), then Turn it on.

entries.t: How do I fill my time sheet every week?
entries.x:
Add your blank time sheet to the Library.
Press Fill my time sheet every week, then Preview.
Tell Sara your shift rules if your calendar has no times, like “shifts are 2200-0700, no lunch”.

entries.t: How do I see why one didn't run?
entries.x:
Press History on its row: each run shows what started it and what each step did.
Three failed runs in a row pause it; fix the problem and switch it back on.
A run waiting for your OK shows Allow and Decline at the top.

entries.t: How do I have her remind me when someone comes up?
entries.x:
In any of your chats, say “when Dan comes up, remind me he owes me $20” (or type /when Dan: he owes me $20).
A card under her reply shows it, with Undo.
The next time you mention Dan in one of your own chats, she brings it up once.
entries.p: Settings → You → When it comes up

entries.t: How do I see or forget what she is waiting to bring up?
entries.x:
Open Planner → Reminders → When it comes up.
Press Forget next to one; Done lists the ones that already came up.
Or type /when for the list and /when forget 1.
entries.p: Settings → You → When it comes up

entries.t: How do I pick up a chat from Telegram in the app?
entries.x:
Open the app after talking on Telegram: a banner offers to pick it up.
Press Continue here (or type /continue in any of your chats).
The chip at the top says where it came from; Undo takes it away.
entries.p: Settings → Connections → Pick up across apps

entries.t: How do I stop the pick-up offers?
entries.x:
Under When I switch apps, choose Only when I type /continue.
To end one pickup, press Undo on its chip (or type /continue off).
entries.p: Settings → Connections → Pick up across apps

entries.t: How do I turn session continuity on or off?
entries.x:
Open Settings → Connections → Apps and services → Pick up across apps → Session continuity.
Switch Use context across my sessions on or off; it saves automatically.
Off stops new context but keeps saved notes. Pick up across apps and While she's working keep their own settings.

entries.t: How do I read the notes from my other sessions?
entries.x:
Close Settings and open one of your own eligible chats with this companion.
Press the conversation chip at the top, then find Saved session context.
Press Show saved session context to see the source, time, expiry and notes.
Notes help later replies; they do not send messages or confirm completed work.

entries.t: How do I clear saved notes, including expired ones?
entries.x:
In This conversation, show the saved session context first.
Choose Clear saved context, review the confirmation, then Confirm clear; Cancel or Escape leaves the notes alone.
Clear also removes expired saved notes while continuity is off; only this session's saved notes are removed.
Original chats, old run records, exports and backups stay.
If the notes changed elsewhere, reload and review them before trying again.

entries.t: How do I add a GitHub token?
entries.x:
Make a token on GitHub (Settings → Developer settings).
Paste it in GitHub token.
Press Save.

entries.t: How do I turn issues into tasks?
entries.x:
Under Issues become tasks, set a label.
Press Look now to fetch them.

entries.t: How do I have her fix a GitHub issue?
entries.x:
Under Fix an issue, type the repository (owner/name) and press Show issues.
Press Fix this issue next to the issue.
Her team fixes it in its own worktree and runs the tests until they pass.
When the card says Ready for your OK, press Open the pull request (or Not now).

entries.t: How do I connect a server?
entries.x:
Type the server address and your user name under Connect a server.
Press Connect and wait while Sara looks at it.
Say yes to its ID card, then follow the way in she picks.
entries.p: Settings → Skills & tools → Servers over SSH

entries.t: How do I connect a cPanel server?
entries.x:
In cPanel, make an API token called sara that expires tomorrow.
Copy it and paste it into the cPanel token box.
Press Install my key: Sara installs her key and deletes the token.
entries.p: Settings → Skills & tools → Servers over SSH

entries.x:
Read the box under the button you pressed.
Press the button it offers, like Find the port or Check now.
entries.p: Settings → Skills & tools → Servers over SSH

entries.t: Does she ask before running commands there?
entries.x:
Yes, every command asks first by default.
Change it in Tools and approvals.
entries.p: Settings → Skills & tools → Servers over SSH

entries.t: How do I share to Sara from my iPhone?
entries.x:
Press Make a token and copy it.
In the Shortcuts app, build Share to Sara with the steps shown here.
Turn on Show in Share Sheet.

entries.t: How do I ask Sara with Siri?
entries.x:
Make a token with Ask Sara on.
Build the Ask Sara shortcut with the steps shown here.
Say "Hey Siri, Ask Sara".

entries.t: How do I put her on my phone?
entries.x:
Open Sara in your phone's browser and sign in.
Press Install Sara as an app (or Add to Home Screen).
Then turn on notifications.

Press Turn on for this device.
Press Send a test.

entries.t: How do I ask her from anywhere?
entries.x:
Pick a Quick ask shortcut.
Press it in any app and type.

entries.t: How do I check notifications work?
entries.x: Press Show a test notification.

entries.t: How do I let her use this computer?
entries.x:
Allow her under This computer.
Choose when she must ask first under Her actions.
Move the mouse to take over any time.

entries.t: How do I stop her right away?
entries.x:
Move the mouse or press a key.
She stops and waits.

entries.t: How do I get her on Telegram?
entries.x:
Press Start and open @BotFather.
Send /newbot and paste the key it gives you.
Press Link my Telegram and send the bot the code.

entries.t: How do I add her to a group?

Her name, pronouns and personality: start from a ready-made character, a guided setup, dials (also for coding), her life. Try her answers first. The character file saves, shares or loads her.
What you are to each other and how she is with you: romance, jealousy, being away, disagreements, intimacy and a stop word. Try her reactions before saving.
How the Sara app behaves on this computer: start when you sign in, keep running next to the clock when you close the window (so she can still reach you), and notifications.
Let her use web pages on this computer in her own browser window: look, read, click and type. Off until you turn it on, and you can stop her any time.
Her work profile for Slack, Teams and other work chats: her work name and tone, work tools only, a separate work memory, and no moods, romance or pictures on her own.
More than one companion on this server: each with her own character, look, voice, conversations and memories. Add, switch and remove them here.
Bring chats from Character.AI, SillyTavern, Replika, Nomi, Kindroid, ChatGPT or Claude: she suggests what she learned, you check it, and only what you keep is saved.

What she looks like in the app. Describe a look (Grok Imagine paints it), dress her in outfits and places, change one thing at a time with her face locked, and keep looks in her closet. Tag closet looks with scenarios and she can dress for the time, the weather and what is happening by herself.
The voice she speaks with (voice notes, read-aloud, calls) and how she hears you. With Grok voice she can laugh, sigh and whisper (Expressive voice); the tone and her mood shape how she sounds.
Say “Hey Sara” and talk, hands-free, in the Windows, Mac or Android app. A small model on the device listens only for her words; nothing is sent until then. Off until you switch it on, per device.
When she may ring you: reminders, finished tasks, the morning briefing; quiet hours and a daily limit. Missed calls become messages.
Pictures she can send you, made with an image model. Off unless you set it up.

Run her model on this computer: Sara finds Ollama, suggests a model that fits your graphics card or memory, and downloads it. The switch Nothing leaves this computer keeps every request on this computer.
The AI model she thinks with in new conversations. Each conversation can use a different one.

Point each job at a model: your best one for talking, a model that can see for pictures, a fast one for background work. Test checks one; Compare… lets you pick the best blind. Backups take over if a model fails.
Use a ChatGPT, Claude or Grok plan you already pay for, where the provider allows it.
Where models come from: Ollama on this or another computer, or a cloud service with an API key. Keys are stored encrypted on your server.
Your name, time zone, language and what you mostly do with her.
How the app looks on this device: palette, Night or Day, color, layout, decoration and her picture.
A morning message with the weather, your list, calendar and important mail, and a weekly review of how things went.
A heads-up when it’s time to leave for calendar events that have an address.
Your business name, address, logo and how to get paid, for the invoices and quotes Sara makes. Plus the currency, tax rate and payment terms she uses by default.
What you type into forms again and again (name, addresses, sizes, vehicle, insurance and loyalty numbers), so Sara can fill web forms in your own browser. Never passwords or card numbers.
Oil changes, tire rotations, furnace filters, gutters and smoke alarms on a schedule, by miles or months. A reminder comes on the day; log a job and the next date moves.
Everything Sara knows about you in one place, by topic, with sources. Search it, ask why, fix or forget anything (with Undo) and merge duplicates; dates in documents can become reminders.
Off by default. Only an adult can turn it on, in a web browser or the desktop app (not the phone apps).
Add-ons from the Sara Store: plugins, skills, tool servers and companions checked by the Sara team. Each shows what it can do before you add it, and nothing switches on by itself.
What she’s allowed to do on her own and what asks you first (running commands, sending mail, pushing code…).
Connect Gmail, Outlook and other mailboxes so she can find mail, draft replies, tidy up and handle your calendar. Sending, organizing and calendar changes ask you first.
Connect Gmail and Calendar so she can find mail, draft replies and handle your calendar. Sending and adding events ask you first.
Connect GitHub so she can commit, push, open pull requests and work with issues. Watch repositories and new issues become tasks.
What she knows about each coding project: commands, layout, rules and her notes. Add a note to teach her something for next time.
Ceilings for each of her replies (tokens, steps, dollars, time), for coding and everyday chats, and what she does near and at the limit.
Reminders that wait for a person or a topic to come up in your own messages (“when Dan comes up, remind me he owes me $20”): how often, how many a day, and when they end.
Everything that runs on its own, in one place: make one from your own words or a starter, preview it, try it without doing anything, switch it on or off and see its history.
Checks after her edits (your project's own type checker or linter, asked once per project) and @-references: attach a file, lines, your changes, the branch, the errors or a web page.
Keep going until it’s done (goals on a chat, ended only by a check you pick) and repeats (checks on a timer in a chat): their caps, quiet hours and daily budgets.
Recipes became skills: everything she saved is in Skills now. This page takes you there.
How-tos she follows for kinds of tasks, in the open Agent Skills format: switch them on or off for this companion, make your own, add skills from other apps, export them.
Installed plugins, five included chat apps, local workflow candidates and starter guides. Candidates use the normal permission review and stay off until enabled for each companion.
Home Assistant: she can see your lights, sensors and thermostat, and change things after you approve.

Connect your other servers so she can work on them over SSH. She makes her own key and finds the easiest way to install it (a cPanel token, the password once, or one pasted line). Every command there asks you first.
How she searches the web for up-to-date answers.

Record totals include finished history. State counts show queued and running work; delivery records can include archived evidence. She writes short notes and remembers facts about you as you talk. A long conversation is noted as it goes, and the last one as soon as you start a new one. See and edit them on the Memory page. She can look back through your past conversations herself. Ask “remember when…”, “what did we say yesterday?” or “what was that lake called?” and she looks it up. At the start of a new conversation she knows how the last one ended. If she can't find something you mention, she says it doesn't come back to her and asks, rather than telling you it never happened (and without making up details). People: …

First you see what's in it: how many conversations and messages, from when to when, a few titles, and what is left out (system prompts, tool and browsing output, hidden reasoning; pictures and attached files are noted but not imported). She shows what's in it: how many conversations and messages, from when to when, and who is who. Set which speaker is you , which is her , and leave out anyone else. Pick the conversa…

Choose her export files (a zip, JSON, CSV, text or a saved chat page, up to 10 files and 50 MB) and paste her backstory, key memories or shared notes. A password-locked zip has to be unzipped first. Her captions: when a photo comes in she writes a short caption in her own voice, from what you two were talking about. Photos from you go to the Looking at pictures model when one can see them. Tiles with nothing in them stay away; Add to your day sets up what is missing. Tiles that read from outside say how f…

Invoices and quotes: say "make an invoice for Rivera Co: 10 hours of design at $85". She numbers it (INV-2026-0001, quotes Q-2026-0001), works out the totals, and makes a PDF or Word file, or fills in your own invoice template from the Library. She never emails it herself; she can write a draft for you to send. Who do I owe a reply: from your connected mailboxes, the people who wrote to you and ar…

Portfolio: share your brokerage's positions export (CSV or Excel from Fidelity, Schwab, Vanguard, Robinhood, E*TRADE…) or type a list like "AAPL 10 @ 150", then ask "how are my stocks doing?". Make a project (+ Project) and give it a workspace: a folder on the server where she reads and writes files. Switch a conversation to coding mode (the button next to the title) for the engineering workflow: she plans, edits, runs tests and shows what changed. Risky actions (running commands, sending mail, pushing code) ask you first . Change that per tool in Settings → Skills & tools → Tools and approvals . With GitHub connected she can commit, push, open pull requests and work with issues.

For every workspace she works in, she keeps a map : each source file, its functions, classes and types (with line numbers), and what imports what. It reads TypeScript and JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, Kotlin, C#, C and C++ (and Markdown headings) with simple rules of her own, so an unusual layout can be missed. It stays up to date by itself: after she writes or edits files, after a job finishes, and with a quick look every few minutes while you work there. Only changed files are read again. Recipes (how she did a tricky job) became skills in 2.29: each one is a skill now, with the same steps and use count, and new ones are saved as skills. See Skills .

entries.t: Sara on your Mac or Windows computer
entries.x: There's a Sara app for Mac and for Windows. It's like the browser version, plus: she keeps running next to the clock (the menu bar on a Mac) when you close the window, so her messages, reminders and calls still reach you; notifications when the window isn't in front (click one to open that conversation); a call brings her window to the front;

You can have several companions on one server. Add one in Settings → Sara → Companions : give a name, pick pronouns, and start from a new character or a copy of one you have. Then switch with ⇄ at the top of the sidebar. Each has her own name, character, look, voice, conversations, memories and diary. A new one shows her initial until you give her a look (Settings → Sara → Look). They share your sign-in, devices, keys, models, tools, add-ons and backups. The planner is shared unless you choose “Each companion keeps her own”. When another companion writes or calls, a small notice appears at …

With two companions or more, press 👥 Group above your conversations to talk with two to four of them at once. Give the chat a title, pick who's in it, and choose who answers. Whoever fits (the default): a quick helper step picks the one or two whose personality fits your message best. Everyone answers : each companion answers, in order. Take turns : one answer per message, going round. @mention only : only who you name answers, for example @Mia (accents and capitals don't matter); without a name, whoever fits. In every style, naming someone with @ asks her. Banter (0 to 2) lets them trade …

It works once. The person opens the link (or I have an invite on the sign-in page), confirms they are 18 or older and gets their own member token, shown once. A skill is a how-to for a kind of task: a folder with a SKILL.md (a name, what it does and when to use it, then the steps) and sometimes notes or scripts beside it. Sara uses the open Agent Skills format, so skills from other apps work in Sara and yours work elsewhere. In every chat with you she sees the name and description of each skill that is on, and opens the one that fits; the line under her reply says Used skill . When one fits clearly, its steps are loaded right away. Partner chats, group chats and other apps get no skills. Six come built in: write a skill, review a pull request, wr…

For bigger jobs, ask her to get the team on it ("get the team to add a dark mode with tests"), or open Team in the sidebar and describe the task. She makes a plan and hands each part to a helper. Helpers each do one job with their own model (from Which model does what ) and tools: 🔎 Researcher, 🧑‍💻 Coder, 🧪 Tester, 🧐 Reviewer, ✍️ Writer, 🎨 Designer, and 🤖 Claude Code / Grok Build. They're not companions: no personality, just a role. Add your own under Helpers and limits . She checks the work: a failing test goes back to the coder, a reviewer's changes too, and a helper that claims so…

entries.t: Plugins: new abilities from a folder
entries.x: A plugin is a small program written for Sara: a folder with a sara-plugin.json and its code. It can give her a tool, add a note before her reply, stop or hold a step for your OK, add a card, run on a schedule, or carry a chat app. Add one in Settings → Skills & tools → Plugins from a .zip, a git address or a folder on the server. Before anything is installed you read its card: what it can do in plain words (riskiest first), its files and its fingerprint. Installing switches nothing on; you switch it on for each companion. An update that asks for more shows the full card again, with the new …

She learns each project: how to build, test and lint it, its layout, its own rules (AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING) and the notes she keeps (decisions, conventions, commands). See and edit them in Settings → Skills & tools → Coding projects . Project checkpoints: keep current logic, blockers and up to three next steps beside a project's notes. Inspect, replace or clear the saved history there, or ask her to save a checkpoint in your own coding chat. A fresh chat in the same unambiguous project can use it after a restart or compaction. This is historical context, not permission to replay commands. …

Ask her for a new project ("build me a Telegram bot", "make me a landing page", "I need a small REST API", "make me a Python command-line tool") and she starts from a tested starter : a Telegram bot, an accessible landing page, a REST API with a built-in database, a command-line tool, or a Python command-line tool. None of them need packages installed. The starter is copied into a new folder in the workspace and its own tests run as a background job, so you both start from something that works. Then she shapes it to what you asked for. Or start one yourself: open a project, press New projec…

entries.t: What Sara knows: your world, with sources

Edit changes her memory too, Delete removes it, and Not true makes her forget it and keeps her from learning it again from the same words. You can also say “forget that I…” in a chat. Every model call that reports its tokens is counted: by model and by what it was for (chat, coding, team, jobs, memory, her life). Every reply, background job and team task keeps a record of how it was done: each step's model, tokens in and out, cost estimate and time, the tools she ran (with what they returned, shortened), whether you allowed them, the files they touched, the memory notes that went in and why, and anything her plan check flagged. Open it with Show the run at the end of a reply's step line. Show what was sent to the model on a step loads exactly what she was given: her instructions (kept once, by fingerprint) and the conversation as it stood. Secrets are hidden before anything is kept. In coding conver…

In Show the run , open a step of a reply and choose Branch from here . Change your message, a result she saw from an earlier step, the notes she remembered (untick one, or add one by its number) or the model, then Run the branch . She carries on from that step with exactly what that step was sent: her instructions as kept, the conversation up to then and the results of the steps before, served from the record (nothing runs again). Your approvals, budgets, the plan check, the sandbox and the safety checks work as in any reply. In coding conversations she works in a copy of your project at th…

entries.t: Evals: which settings work best for you
entries.x: Open Evals in the sidebar (under More). Pick where the tasks come from (your coding conversations by default), how many (the newest, up to 50) and up to three variants : another way of fading old memories, another model (also one on this computer), another sandbox setting or another budget. Only your own finished replies are used, and only ones that can be graded: by your project's tests, by what you said next (“thanks, it works” or a correction), or by the optional second opinion. Off-the-record chats are never used; private ones only when every model is on this computer. The list is froze…

Each reply has a ceiling, so a long task can't run on and on. Coding chats have one by default: 200k tokens and 40 steps , no dollar limit. Everyday chats have none unless you turn it on (they still stop after 25 steps, as before). Change both in Settings → Models & usage → Usage and costs → Budgets , or switch them off. Near the limit she saves instead of running on: first the rest of the reply goes to your quick model (if one is set and it's cheaper), then she uses one more round of tools at most, then she writes a short summary without tools : what's done, what she didn't get to, and wha…

entries.t: Keep going until it's done, and repeats
entries.x: Keep going until it's done: in a chat, press + → Keep going until it’s done… (or type /goal make the tests pass ). Pick what has to pass under Done when : the project's tests, its build or lint, a command you type, a reviewer model, or I'll say . Press Start . She works in rounds. After each round Sara runs the check , not she; if it fails, the next round gets the real failure. It ends done (the check's output is the proof), done, review it (green, but she changed test files: look first), stuck (the same failure again, or a round that changed nothing) or paused at a cap. Her own words never…

entries.t: When it comes up, and picking a chat up in another app
entries.x: When it comes up: say “when Dan comes up, remind me he owes me $20” in any of your chats (or type /when Dan: he owes me $20 ). The next time you mention Dan in one of your own chats, she brings it up once in her reply; the ⏰ chip under it has Done , Again next time and Forget . Only your own messages in your own chats set them off: never shared rooms, other people's chats, private or off-the-record chats, other apps or speakers. Anything she would send to someone else that mentions it asks you first. Pick it up in another app: after talking on Telegram, open the app and press Continue here …

Type / at the start of the message box and a list opens: /goal , /loop , /compact , /tools , /when , /btw , /stop and more, each with one line on what it does. ↑ ↓ and Enter pick one; Esc closes the list. The same commands work in Telegram, Discord and the other chat apps; you only see the ones you may use in that chat. Type @ to point her at a file or a web page. Full list: docs/CHATS.md .

When a chat gets long, /compact (or Tidy this chat on her panel) folds the older part into a summary she reads instead. Your last turns stay word for word, the folded messages stay in the thread under a divider with Show summary and Undo , and nothing is deleted. Private chats are only ever tidied by a model on this computer. Full guide: docs/TOOLS_AND_COMPACT.md .

Planner → Routines has ready-made things she does on a schedule: a morning briefing, a weekly review, a reminder to stretch, a CI watch and more. Each card says when it runs, what it needs and what it costs, and shows a preview before Turn on . Off stops a routine at once. Full guide: docs/ROUTINES.md . Watch a file (in Planner → Routines ): pick a log or file in one of your workspaces, or Sara’s own log, and a few words like ERROR . She tells you about new matching lines in a chat card and a notification; each watch has Check now , Pause and Stop . Reading costs nothing, and she never fixe…

entries.t: Commands tried in a sandbox first
entries.x: In coding conversations (and for her team's helpers), a command that could change your project first runs in a throwaway copy of the workspace. Read-only commands such as ls , cat or git status pass straight through; commands that write, install, delete, use the network or run a script are tried first. The card Ran in a sandbox shows the command, its result and time, the files it added, changed or removed, and anything worth a look: writes outside the copy, many files deleted, git hooks, network use, programs left running (they are stopped), running out of time. You choose: Apply to my work…

After a coding turn that changed files, she checks those files in the background for common security mistakes: secrets written into code, eval or shell commands built from input, SQL built by joining strings, file paths taken from a request, certificate checks turned off, unsafe loading of data, any website allowed with cookies, a new route without the sign-in check the others use, weak hashing for passwords or tokens, HTML built from input and debug mode left on. Every finding quotes the real line it is about. A second look by the Reviewing model (Which model does what; the Coding model wh…

entries.t: Threat model and the fix pass
entries.x: After a coding turn that changed files, she maps where your app can be reached from ( entry points : web routes, file uploads, messages, the command line) and follows each one through your own functions to dangerous lines : shell commands, SQL, file paths, outgoing requests, unsafe loading of data, HTML, redirects, code that runs input. A route that changes things without a sign-in check, or a sign-in route without a rate limit, counts too. Each threat quotes its entry point and the dangerous line and names the path between them; a check on the way (placeholders, keeping only the file name,…

entries.t: Red team: try to break it before you ship
entries.x: Red-team this (in Findings → Red team , on the card under a coding reply, or Before you ship on the project page) first shows the plan: the entry points, how many unusual inputs, the tests, how the app is started, the budget and the time limit. Nothing runs until you press Start . Everything runs in a throwaway copy of the project with the network off: the project's tests; the app started on a free local port; generic unusual input at every entry point (empty, very long, unusual Unicode, path-like text, quotes, numbers out of range, wrong types, missing or duplicated fields, malformed JSON)…

With the Sara app for Windows or Mac, Sara can use her own browser window on your computer: open pages, read them, take screenshots and read console and network errors, and click, type, choose in lists, press keys, scroll and upload a file you named. Handy when your web app is broken or a form needs filling in. It's off until you switch on Let Sara use this computer in the app (Settings → Computer use). The first time it explains what she can do and asks you to confirm it's you. She uses her own browser window with its own profile: never your browser, tabs or passwords. A pink frame shows w…

Press 🎲 next to the message box: 20 questions , trivia , would you rather , journal together (she asks about your day and writes a short entry you can save), watch along (tell her what you're watching) and a story together . A bar above the message box shows what you're doing; press End to stop. Shared lists : a playlist, a reading list and a watch list you both add to. Tell her about a song or show and she can add it; she suggests her own too. She remembers what's coming up in your life and asks how it went afterwards ("how did the interview go?"), within her quiet hours and daily limits.

Look: describe one and Grok Imagine paints it, with matching expressions and animation ( Settings → Sara → Look ). See her large: tap or click her picture. Zoom with a pinch, the scroll wheel or a double tap; swipe or use the arrows to go through her expressions and closet; save or share a picture. Outfits and places: dress her for the season or the day, and put her somewhere else (her room, a café, the office, outdoors, the beach…). You see a picture first. Change one thing: hair, eyes, makeup, glasses, accessories, tattoos, body type, height or the art style, without starting over.

The search box above the conversations looks through everything: conversations, memories, notes, to-dos, the scrapbook and project files. Ask about anything in your life: type in the search box and pick the first row (✦). One question goes to your emails, files, chats, calendars, notes, lists and contacts; the answer quotes each source with a number you can tap to open it. Private chats are never searched. Tags: ⋯ next to a conversation → Tags. Tap a tag under the search box to see only those. Pins: 📌 under a message keeps it at the top of the conversation.

Backups run every day on the server. Add an off-server copy (a folder or S3-compatible storage like Backblaze B2), encrypted with your passphrase, in Settings → Privacy & system → Backups . Updates: Settings → Privacy & system → Updates checks for a new version and installs it. A backup is made first, and if the new version doesn't start, Sara goes back to the one she had by herself. On the server: sudo sara update . Health shows whether everything is working, and why not. Restore a backup on the server: sudo sara restore <file> .

The owner token is the master key to your Sara. Keep it in a password manager; don't share it. New devices don't need the token: Settings → Connections → Devices and sign-in → Add a phone or computer makes a one-time code that works for 10 minutes. Passkeys (same page): sign in with your fingerprint, face or device PIN. Nothing secret leaves your device. Two-step sign-in (same page): signing in with the token also asks for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app.

Sara is an AI. She says so when you start, every few hours, and whenever you sincerely ask. If you mention being in crisis she points you to real help (in the US, call or text 988 ). Sexual content involving minors is always blocked, whatever the model or settings. If a reply is offensive or harmful, use ⚑ under it to report it.

Open Settings → Privacy & system → Health : it checks every model and says what's wrong (wrong key, the computer running Ollama is off, the subscription signed out…). On the server run sudo sara reset-token for a new owner token (this signs out every browser; the phone apps sign in again with a new code). Check the server address (it must start with https:// ), and that the server is running: sudo sara status . See the support page .

To report a problem from inside Sara, open Help → Report a problem (or Suggest something ), or type /bug or /idea in the chat. An error notice has a Report this link that fills the error in. You can add diagnostics. They are made on your computer and shown in full first, with a tick for each part; keys, emails and your folder names are hidden. Nothing goes until you press Send . Help → My reports shows what you sent, its status and the team's replies, and you can answer there. Sara also sends an anonymous daily check-in you can switch off: the version, the kind of computer and which feature…

Settings → Privacy & system → Privacy → What left this server lists, per day, every request this server sent out: the place (like api.openai.com), why it went (AI models, web search, mail…), how many and about how much was sent. Only the place and a count are kept, for 30 days. What was in a request (your messages, mail, search words) is never written down. Things that only connect to this computer, like a model running here, are not listed. With Nothing leaves this computer on, the list stays empty and shows what was stopped instead.
